summary.headline: Sundrop Brands Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY (11% QoQ) with EBITDA steady at about 7% of sales, net of ESOP.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY and 11% QoQ, with B2B up 18% and e-commerce up 32%. Gross margin improved about 110 bps despite commodity and packaging inflation, and EBITDA held at about 7%, the same level as Q4 FY26. A&P was reported about 12% lower YoY, but management says about 5% lower on a like-for-like basis after reclassifying trade spends as contra-revenue. Management reiterated a target of 300 bps annual margin expansion and about 12% EBITDA by FY30, with 200 bps from Del Monte-Sundrop synergies over 18 months.

financial_highlights.value: Up about 110 bps (stated as overall margin improvement)
financial_highlights.change: Material cost efficiency +40 bps; other expenses +70 bps
Same as Q4 FY26; ESOP-burdened about 5.66%

financial_highlights.value: About 12% lower YoY as reported; about 5% lower like-for-like (21.4 vs 22.9 as % of sales)
financial_highlights.change: Reclassification of trade spends to contra-revenue; like-for-like growth about 12% QoQ

financial_highlights.value: About 56% of total business, growing about 16%
About 44-45% of total business, growing about 14%

financial_highlights.change: Q4 FY26 share of business about 62%

segments.name: Popcorn
segments.commentary: Growing about 18% with about 12% volume growth; Ready-to-Eat growing about 39% (vs 33% last year) while Ready-to-Cook grows about 9%. Management says it holds about 85% category share.

segments.name: Culinary (ketchup, mayo, dressings)
segments.commentary: Growth accelerated to 15% from about 10% last year, with volume growth of about 8%; B2B and exports to Southeast Asia contributing.

segments.name: Premium staples / edible oil
segments.commentary: Value growth about 16% and volume growth about 7%, with about 9% of growth from price pass-through; oil is about 20% of total business. Management targets 4-5% volume growth.

segments.name: Italian (olive oil, pasta, RTE olives)
segments.commentary: Value growth returned to about 8% and volume to 15-17%; olive oil volume grew close to 20%, pasta about 10%. Q1 realisations fell due to prior-year commodity deflation pass-through.

segments.name: Peanut butter / spreads
segments.commentary: Decline narrowed to about 3% in value and volume from 8-10% last year; e-commerce returned to 16% growth. Market is about 85% value-added; company holds about 33% of standard and 3% of value-added peanut butter.

segments.name: Juices
segments.commentary: Investment dropped; management says it was not core and did not show good results.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for mid-teens to high-teens revenue growth, with about 10% volume growth, 4-5% value growth from pricing and 4-5% from innovation as the long-term mix.
EBITDA target of about 12% by FY30 (about three years), from about 7% ESOP-adjusted today; ESOP cost to stay front-loaded for 18-21 months.

Overall ambition of about 300 bps annual margin expansion, split half reinvested in growth and half returned to shareholders; about 100 bps a year from scale, 80-100 bps from premiumisation and about 100 bps a year from synergies over two years.
Del Monte and Sundrop synergies estimated at about 200 bps, delivered over about 18 months; about 8 CFA consolidations targeted by end of this year, leaving 2 of Del Monte's 10 unique CFAs.
Italian business: value growth expected to move closer to 15% if volume growth of 15% is sustained; price stabilisation expected from Q2.
Single ERP for both businesses to be decided soon, with migration expected within about 12 months, before sales-force integration.
capex_capacity: Shift to a capital-efficient model: using third-party manufacturing and outsourced systems in place of own capex; management also says it is actively looking at inorganic opportunities.
Popcorn facilities at Kashipur and Kothur are running at rising utilisation, adding to profitability on instant popcorn.
Ready-to-Eat assorted manufacturing is improving plant utilisation and freight efficiency; direct factory-to-distributor shipping cuts freight and shelf-life packaging cost (4.5-5 month shelf life).
Salesforce automation: about 80% of outlets now billed on the platform, up from about 75% at the end of Q4 FY26.
demand_pricing: Edible oil: volume 7%, value about 15-16%, with about 9% from pass-through of per-kg price increases; management is now growing volume and aims for 4-5% volume growth.
Peanut butter: management says the market has moved to about 85% value-added formats (protein, chocolate, natural) where it has about 3% share; competition includes PE-backed brands.
Popcorn Rs. 10 RTC/RTE packs are expanding into East, West and South; e-commerce growth is led by Rs. 25-50 MRP packs, with bigger packs now about 36% of RTE mix (from about 33%).
Premium staples: management says it has a lower-priced variant (Sundrop Lite and Sundrop Heart Plus) as a safety net if sunflower oil inflation drives consumers down.
Italian realisation down about 6-10% in Q1 due to higher old-price inventory being sold after last year's commodity deflation; not quick-commerce discounting per management.

qa_highlights.question: Navin (Ithought PMS): Is the YoY dip in A&P a genuine efficiency gain or a shift in focus across brands/segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said focus stayed on core categories invested since Q4 FY25 (Sundrop) and Q1 FY26 (Del Monte); Juices was dropped as non-core. Reported A&P down about 12% YoY, but after reclassifying trade spends to contra-revenue it is 21.4 vs 22.9 of sales, about 5% lower.

qa_highlights.question: Navin: Post the 4700BC acquisition by a large player, is there more competitive aggression in popcorn and what differs from ACT II's offerings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management holds about 85% popcorn category share and has not seen a significant shift in category behaviour since the acquisition. It has raised investment, is pushing Sweet Popcorn, and has added Cheese popcorn to e-commerce.

qa_highlights.question: Pritesh Chheda (Lucky Investments): What are the blended volume and value growth rates for core and non-core?
qa_highlights.answer: Core (about 60% of sales) grows about 14-15% in value and 9-10% in volume. Edible oil (about 20% of business) grew about 16% in value and 7% in volume. The remaining ~20% grows about 15% in value and 8% in volume, helped by CP manufacturing such as energy drinks. Overall, about 80% of the business grows 15-16% in value and 8-9% in volume.

qa_highlights.question: Pritesh Chheda: What are the key growth pillars and the expected value and volume mix?
qa_highlights.answer: For Popcorn, Ketchup and Mayo the pillars are distribution, media investment ahead of curve, and innovation; Italian is driven more by innovation and investment, and peanut butter by innovation. Management sees about 4-5% volume growth in most categories and aims for about 10% volume, plus 4-5% price and 4-5% innovation, targeting mid-teens to high-teens growth.

qa_highlights.question: Balaji Vaidyanath (Nafa Asset Management): Is the 6-10% Italian realisation decline due to quick-commerce discounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Kapoor said no. Q1 is running on higher-cost inventory bought before last year's commodity deflation, with price pass-through having started only in Q2 last year. Prices are now stabilising and the effect should end from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Balaji Vaidyanath: Is GT/MT growth likely low single digit given B2B at 18% and e-commerce at 32%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Popcorn, Italian and oil are primarily retail. Culinary is the only mixed retail and B2B business. B2B grows faster than retail, and retail is roughly 10-12% if B2B is at 18%. The company did not give a specific GT/MT number.

qa_highlights.question: Balaji Vaidyanath: How much of the 15% edible oil growth is price pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Asheesh Sharma said about 9 points is price pass-through (per-kg increase passed on almost fully) with 7% volume, giving roughly 16% value growth.

qa_highlights.question: Percy Panthaki (IIFL Capital): What is the status of the Del Monte and Sundrop integration, and what savings are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce is under a single operations team. Del Monte had 10 unique CFAs, with 2 already consolidated and a third underway; about 8 consolidations are targeted by year-end, leaving 2. ERP migration to a single system is expected within about 12 months, before sales-force integration. East distribution of Del Monte already runs through the Sundrop team. Synergies are about 200 bps over 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Percy Panthaki: EBITDA goes from about 7% to about 12% in three years. What is the breakup beyond the 200 bps synergies?
qa_highlights.answer: ESOP cost (about 5.66% after ESOP) is front-loaded for 18-21 months, adding roughly 100 bps after that. Scale is worth about 100 bps a year, premiumisation 80-100 bps a year, and synergies about 100 bps a year for two years. Management aims for about 300 bps of margin expansion a year, split half to growth and half to shareholders. FY30 12% is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Shirish Pardeshi (Motilal Oswal): What is the economics and sustainability of the Rs. 10 popcorn RTC/RTE packs and their supply chain?
qa_highlights.answer: Assorted manufacturing and direct factory-to-distributor shipping cut freight and packaging cost, with a 4.5-5 month shelf life. RTE Rs. 10 has moved from margin-dilutive to margin-accretive over 18 months. Bigger packs are about one-third of the RTE mix (from one-fifth/one-third earlier), growing 42% against 33% for the rest, and e-commerce is growing about 55%.

qa_highlights.question: Shirish Pardeshi: Will premium staples volume (7%) hold if sunflower inflation drives price up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to lower-priced variants as a safety net: Sundrop Lite and Sundrop Heart Plus, with a new Sundrop Heart blend using less-inflated commodities. It targets 4-5% volume growth in the category, which is growing about 3-4%. The Sundrop Heart Jodi pack will continue through the festive season.

qa_highlights.question: Nachiket Kale (Emkay): What is the strategy for peanut butter given competition from new digital-first and PE-backed brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it lost the protein, natural and chocolate variant race because it lacked those products. The market is about 85% value-added and 15% standard. The company holds about 33% of standard and 3% of value-added peanut butter. It is launching new variants, investing in digital consumer acquisition, and aims for double-digit growth in the near term.

risks_watch: A&P optics: reported A&P is down about 12% YoY, but like-for-like is about 5% lower after the contra-revenue reclassification. Watch whether reclassification distorts sales and margin comparisons.
Input cost inflation in edible oil (sunflower), packaging and commodities. Management says price pass-through has so far protected margins, but B2B and some contracts have lagged price increases.
Peanut butter: still in decline at about 3% in value and volume, with only 3% share of value-added formats against 85% of the market. Competition from digital-first and PE-backed brands.
Italian business: realisation down 6-10% in Q1 from old inventory. Management expects stabilisation from Q2 and value growth of about 15% if volume growth holds at 15%.
Integration execution: CFA consolidation (about 8 targeted by year-end), ERP migration within about 12 months, and sales-force integration. Synergies of about 200 bps over 18 months.

Margin path to about 12% EBITDA by FY30 depends on ESOP cost rolling off after 18-21 months and on premiumisation and scale. Juices has been dropped as non-core, and any further portfolio exits or inorganic moves are open questions.
key_quotes: So, we are a tad higher, I would say sharply higher also than 4%, which we used to be about a year and a half back.
We have lost out that race because we did not have any of that product in the portfolio.
Our overall endeavor is to improve our margins by 300 basis points every year, of which we would want to deploy half back to the business and half back to the shareholders.
Our stated position on this category will be to protect volumes.
So, we will have to play the game as it is being played, that we are cognizant of.
summary.management_tone: Confident and growth-focused on top-line momentum, B2B, e-commerce and popcorn. More cautious and evasive on peanut butter recovery, the Italian realisation dip, and the detailed bridge from 7% to 12% EBITDA, which management frames as a three-year target. Management often answered questions by restating broad ambitions rather than giving precise numbers.
